summary: The first of BBN's regular reports on how available ARPANET hosts were, based on talks with sites and daily test logins from a prototype Terminal IMP. It lists hosts excluded from testing. This version had many typing errors and was reissued as RFC 240.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 235 reports ARPANET host status for September 13 through September 24, 1971. It combines information from site contacts with daily login tests from a BBN Terminal IMP.

questions: how did bbn test host availability
what hosts were available on the arpanet
what do the rfc 235 status codes mean
subtitle: A BBN report combines operator information with daily host login tests.

tldr.problem: Network users needed regular information about which ARPANET hosts were available as servers.
tldr.mechanism: BBN combined information from site contacts with weekday login attempts from a prototype Terminal IMP and published host status tables.
tldr.outcome: RFC 235 begins reports about host availability and was replaced by RFC 240, according to the unit metadata.

today: RFC 235 was obsoleted by RFC 240. It is a snapshot of ARPANET host status for September 13 through September 24, 1971.

sections.title: How the Status Information Was Gathered
sections.content: RFC 235 says BBN would report the status of most network hosts about once every two weeks. Information came from talking with people at each site and from daily login attempts made at random times on weekdays by BBN's prototype Terminal IMP.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN asked site operators about their hosts and tried to log in each day. This report covers the period from September 13 through September 24.

sections.title: Hosts Excluded from Daily Tests
sections.content: The report excludes hosts not expected to function as servers for at least a month and hosts intended only as users. The second group includes Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center computer, which the RFC says was used solely to gather network statistics.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN did not test every host. It excluded hosts not expected to serve others soon and hosts intended only to use the network.

sections.title: Reading the Test Results
sections.content: The report's tables list host status at test times during the reporting period. “D” means dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP, “R” means refused, “T” means timed out, “1/2 O” means a connection opened but then closed or stopped responding, and “O” means open and accessible.
sections.plainLanguage: The letters summarize what happened during a test. “O” means the host was accessible; other codes describe no response, refusal, timeout, or a connection that stopped early.
